Turn the supplied photo into a single minimalist geometric art print on light neutral ivory paper, landscape 3:2. Use only the visible subject matter in the photo. For a person or animal, make the figure the main graphic and preserve subject count, pose, facing direction, and the few visible details that distinguish it, such as hairstyle, distinctive clothing, the placement of coat markings, or a collar. Keep an uncluttered indoor or studio background as bare paper. For a landscape, let the dominant landform, structure, or water shape be the subject, and keep the relationships among the visible landforms and water. In a mixed scene, keep the principal subject and the most distinctive part of its setting. Include a supporting object or landscape feature only when it is visible in the source and helps identify the scene. Do not invent scenery, objects, figures, or a context like travel or sport. Abstract construction lines are fine.

Compose the selected shapes as one compact graphic centered on the page, with generous uninterrupted ivory paper around it. Allow the sky, ground, and unneeded background to disappear into the bare paper. Build the image from broad flat circles, triangles, stepped silhouettes, and repeated arcs. Simplify faces or muzzles to a few recognizable shapes, clothing to solid planes, and props to clean silhouettes. Omit incidental details, folds, fur strands, foliage texture, realistic shadows, gradients, and photoreal detail. Use three or four muted inks, with the source's strongest color as a focal accent. Add a few faint construction lines aligned to the artwork, a small row of ink swatches, and an understated one- to three-word title describing what can actually be seen. Use generic descriptive words and no proper names, place names, or inferred activities. Keep the ivory paper nearly smooth with faint matte print grain. No frame, inset border, photo panel, mockup, logos, or watermark. Return only the completed print.
